title: Three-dimensional deformation prediction and monitoring optimization for open-pit mine slopes
subtitle: Slope monitoring & forecasting
shortTitle: Three-dimensional deformation prediction and monitoring optimization for open-pit mine slopes
summary: Monitoring open-pit mine slopes requires identifying the spatial distribution and evolution of deformation, but sparsely distributed GNSS monitoring points commissioned at different times provide observations only at limited locations. This study integrates displacement histories from target and neighboring monitoring points with terrain information to develop a spatiotemporal model for three-dimensional displacement prediction. It provides both central displacement predictions and upper prediction limits for displacement magnitude to balance prediction accuracy with the identification of areas of larger deformation. Combining the predicted deformation field with the spatial coverage of the monitoring network further yields a monitoring-point optimization scheme involving priority retention, supplementary coverage, and redundancy review.

blocks.text: Monitoring open-pit mine slopes requires identifying the spatial distribution and evolution of deformation, but sparsely distributed GNSS monitoring points commissioned at different times provide observations only at limited locations. Combining the predicted deformation field with the spatial coverage of the monitoring network further yields a monitoring-point optimization scheme involving priority retention, supplementary coverage, and redundancy review.

media.alt: Three-dimensional deformation prediction and estimation at continuous spatial locations
media.label: Figure 1 Three-dimensional deformation prediction and estimation at continuous spatial locations
media.caption: Displacement histories from target and neighboring monitoring points and terrain information jointly inform spatiotemporal prediction, and point-based results are then extended to continuous spatial locations. Central displacement predictions describe the main movement, while upper prediction limits for displacement magnitude are used to screen for larger deformation.

media.alt: Prediction of displacement magnitude at monitoring points
media.label: Figure 2 Prediction of displacement magnitude at monitoring points
media.caption: Central displacement predictions underestimate magnitudes for samples with larger displacements. Upper prediction limits for displacement magnitude, calibrated using residuals from high-deformation samples, increase coverage of large-magnitude movements.

media.alt: Future displacement increments across the area
media.label: Figure 3 Future displacement increments across the area
media.caption: Future displacement increments are concentrated on localized slope surfaces and benches, with high-value areas varying with the forecast horizon. Central displacement predictions and upper prediction limits for displacement magnitude respectively represent the main movement and the areas warranting attention for larger deformation.

blocks.text: Monitoring-point optimization combines regional deformation and spatial coverage. While retaining key locations and critical continuous records, it adds monitoring points in underrepresented areas and reviews proposed adjustments to redundant observations.

media.alt: Monitoring-point layout jointly constrained by area coverage and key locations
media.label: Figure 4 Monitoring-point layout jointly constrained by area coverage and key locations
media.caption: Regional representativeness, key deformation locations, and distinct movement zones jointly constrain the monitoring configuration. Additional monitoring locations are identified and redundant observations reviewed while maintaining spatial coverage.
